solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Savage treatment, as yet unknown by dear Parisian

parts.note: 'but' can mean 'as yet', as in 'had but begun'
cher is French for dear, as a Parisian would say it
Y is an algebraic unknown, like X

explanation.surface: Someone is cruelly treated, without knowing it, by a beloved Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the unknown next to the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchery is brutal slaughter or cruel mutilation, a savage way of treating people.

clue.text: Support parts of the borough going in reverse

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a borough is divided into electoral wards

explanation.surface: Supporting local districts is a step backwards for the council.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving backwards is travelling in the opposite direction, the adverb matching 'going in reverse'.

clue.text: Tiles which start to slide — work to stop that

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the start of the word slide gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Roof tiles are starting to slip, and repair work should prevent it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiles' is old slang for hats, so it does not mean roofing here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tile is dated British slang for a hat, and the formal silk hat is the classic example.

clue.text: Rock in river?

parts.note: Rock is the first name of the film star whose surname also names New York's great river

explanation.surface: A boulder sitting in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock Hudson was a Hollywood actor; the river through New York shares his surname, so 'Rock' is in the river's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of actor Rock Hudson is also the name of the American river, so the river contains Rock.

clue.text: Legal right about to be written on form

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is written on top of the second

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a version is one form of something

explanation.surface: A lawyer's note about a right that must be entered on an official form.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a reversion is the right to get property back once a lease or grant ends.

clue.text: Shelter, for example, to accommodate most of the characters in gala

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: 'say' introduces an example, as in 'a fruit, say, an apple'

indicators.note: most of means dropping the final letter of the word

parts.note: a gala is a fete, and those are the letters taken

explanation.surface: A refuge laid on to house most of the people at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gala' is the usual crossword route to a fete; 'most of' then drops its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety is a state or place of protection, the same sense as shelter from danger.

clue.text: Agreed to put soldiers into detachment

indicators.note: into means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a squad is a small detachment of troops
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: An officer consented to posting troops into a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts or stories that squared were consistent, so they agreed with each other.

clue.text: Mate entertains powerless chums turning up in Dutch province

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters backwards
P stands for power, so the word loses that letter

parts.note: chums are pals

explanation.surface: A friend hosts some feeble chums arriving in a Netherlands region.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the standard abbreviation for power, so 'powerless' removes it; 'turning up' reverses what is left, as in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Friesland is a northern province of the Netherlands, home of the Frisian language.

clue.text: Country with revolutionary enthusiast is the reverse of excellent

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a nut is a fan or enthusiast
taken as written

indicators.note: the reverse of means the letters run the other way

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI

explanation.surface: A nation with a radical zealot in charge is far from first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African nation on the Mediterranean, so it is a country.

clue.text: Limit an EU policy

definitions.meaning: the Common Agricultural Policy of the European Union

explanation.surface: A call to restrict a European Union programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap is a ceiling, and CAP is the initials of the Common Agricultural Policy.

clue.text: Last thing Scotland needs, change? It has it already!

definitions.text: Last thing Scotland needs, change? It has it already!

indicators.note: the last thing in a word is its final letter

parts.note: evolution is gradual change

explanation.surface: A wry remark that Scotland hardly needs more change, since it already has its own parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland got its own parliament in 1999, so the transfer of powers it 'needs' is already in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Devolution is the transfer of powers from central government to a region, which Scotland received with its parliament.

clue.text: Way person, having lost son, waves about arms

indicators.note: waving something about throws it around, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: having lost means the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone on the road, missing a child, flails about with their arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' takes S from PERSON to leave PERON; 'waves about' shuffles WAY and PERON together.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms means weapons collectively, and weaponry is the word for weapons as a group.

clue.text: Stand up against support one's brought in

indicators.note: brought in means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a rest is a support, as in an armrest
one's is read as one (I) plus is (S), giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to accept the backing that has been imported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is': I for one and the S of 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or withstand, the same as standing up against something.

clue.text: Explorer went up south, rather than west side of Everest

indicators.note: rather than means one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: rose means went up

indicators.note: on a map the west side is the left, so the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A mountaineer climbed the south face of Everest instead of the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rather than' swaps the E of ROSE for S.
explanation.definitionFit: James Clark Ross was a British polar explorer after whom the Ross Sea and Ross Ice Shelf are named.

clue.text: Farm worker offers drink in bit of broken pottery

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a sherd, or shard, is a fragment of broken pottery
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: A labourer serves wine in a broken piece of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A swineherd is someone who tends pigs, a traditional job on a farm.

clue.text: Kicking the drug habit, nevertheless admitting attraction

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: withal is an old word for nevertheless
a draw is an attraction, something that pulls crowds

explanation.surface: A recovering addict who admits the drug still appeals.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming off drugs is called withdrawal, the process and its symptoms after stopping use.

clue.text: One who welcomes bloke, not wanting female type of holidaymaker

parts.note: a host welcomes guests

indicators.note: not wanting means doing without, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: feller is a casual word for a man or bloke

explanation.surface: A host greets a man, as he doesn't want a woman at the guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who travels staying in youth hostels is a kind of holidaymaker.

clue.text: Drunk upset majestic group outside university

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: regal means majestic

indicators.note: outside means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A disturbed royal party gathers outside a college.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunk is an intoxicated person, and this British term names a young man rowdy from beer.

clue.text: Harshness of tone in quiet customer's last complaint

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: last here asks for the final letter of the word customer, ignoring the possessive

parts.note: a complaint is an ailment or illness

explanation.surface: A shop customer's final grumble, made in a hushed but grating voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' means an ailment, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrillness is a high, piercing quality of sound, which is a harsh tone.

clue.text: Henry apt to imprison wife, the idiot!

parts.note: Hal is a short form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

indicators.note: to imprison is to hold inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: fit means apt or suitable

explanation.surface: An exclamation about Henry VIII locking up a wife: what a fool!
explanation.definitionFit: A halfwit is a foolish or stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Port enlivened a talk with first signs of inebriation apparent

indicators.note: enlivened suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first signs of means the opening letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A port wine livened up a conversation as signs of drunkenness appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enlivened' rearranges A TALK into LATAK. 'Port' suggests the drink in the surface, but here it is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Latakia is the main seaport of Syria, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Trail of paper at back of yard

indicators.note: at places the next piece right after the other
the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A trail of newspaper litter behind the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: In hunting a drag is an artificial scent trail laid for the hounds to follow.

clue.text: Novel in genuine setting? Library users may want that

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: real means genuine
novel means new

explanation.surface: A novel with an authentic backdrop is one borrowers will request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, which fits the library, but it means new.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowers who want to keep a book longer ask for a renewal of the loan.

clue.text: University procedure to get degree needing endless deception

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trick is a deception

explanation.surface: Getting a degree requires a constant stream of fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Matric, short for matriculation, is the formal process of enrolling at a university.

clue.text: Subtle changes making one most depressed

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Small alterations can leave a person at their lowest.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means sad or low, so its superlative is the saddest, most depressed.

clue.text: Message of royalist who works in household maybe?

definitions.meaning: keep the Queen, ER being Elizabeth Regina
a servant attached to a household

explanation.surface: A servant in a grand house is probably a monarchist with a slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, so the slogan 'retain ER' is a royalist message.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a long-serving servant of a family or household.

clue.text: Little plant needing to absorb potassium — hesitation to provide garden chemical

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

indicators.note: to absorb is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: dill is a herb plant
K is the chemical symbol for potassium
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A small plant needs potash, so a gardener hesitates before reaching for a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbicide sprayed on unwanted plants is a chemical used in gardens.

clue.text: International organisation's question of identity

definitions.meaning: the World Health Organization, a United Nations agency
the question word asking which person someone is

explanation.surface: A global body asking who it really is.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the initials of the World Health Organization and also the word asking which person.

clue.text: Places of entertainment remained here, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say signals that the words are heard spoken, not seen

parts.note: remained means stayed, and here said with a dropped H

explanation.surface: A guest asks whether someone stayed at this venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic accent with the H dropped, 'stayed 'ere' sounds like the plural of stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia, the plural of stadium, are arenas where sport and shows entertain crowds.

clue.text: Band in British competition facing impediment

parts.note: a race is a competition
let is an old word for hindrance, as in tennis or 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A musical group competing in a British contest faces an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band worn round the wrist.
